subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Belief that God is the creator means Jews understand that God:
options: Only created human beings, not the world
Is one of many forces that shaped the world
Brought the universe into being and sustains it
Created the world but then ceased to exist
questions.explain: Jews believe God is the creator who brought the universe into being and continues to sustain it.

questions.q: Who was prepared to sacrifice his son Isaac in obedience to God?
questions.explain: Abraham showed faith when he was willing to sacrifice Isaac, before God provided a ram instead.

questions.q: Which prophet is regarded in Judaism as the greatest, who spoke with God 'face to face'?
questions.explain: Moses is regarded as the greatest prophet in Judaism, through whom God gave the Torah.

questions.q: Which collection of scriptures is known by the acronym Tenakh?
questions.explain: The Tenakh is made up of the Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings).

questions.q: In Judaism, God is described as the lawgiver because God:
options: Allows people to invent their own laws freely
Gave the Torah and its commandments to guide people
Punishes without any rules or fairness
Lives inside the Temple and nowhere else
questions.explain: Jews believe God is the lawgiver who revealed the Torah and its commandments to direct how people should live.

questions.q: What is the building where Jews gather for communal worship called?
questions.explain: The synagogue is the Jewish place of communal worship, study and gathering.

questions.q: The Shema teaches Jews to love God with all their heart, soul and:
questions.explain: The Shema commands love of God with all one's heart, soul and might (strength).

questions.q: What is the central Jewish declaration of faith beginning 'Hear, O Israel'?
questions.explain: The Shema declares belief in one God and is a central statement of Jewish faith.

questions.q: Where did Moses receive the Ten Commandments?
questions.explain: Moses received the Torah and the Ten Commandments from God at Mount Sinai.

questions.q: How many mitzvot (commandments) does the Torah traditionally contain?
questions.explain: The Torah traditionally contains 613 mitzvot that guide Jewish life.

questions.q: What is the special meal eaten during Pesach called?
questions.explain: The Seder is the special Passover meal at which the story of the Exodus is retold.

questions.q: What is Shabbat in Judaism?
questions.explain: Shabbat is the weekly day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday evening, recalling God resting after creation.

questions.q: What does Judaism teach about the number of gods?
options: There are two equal gods, good and evil
questions.explain: Judaism is strictly monotheistic, believing in one God who is the creator of everything.

questions.q: The covenant at Sinai is often called the Mosaic covenant because it was made through:
questions.explain: The Sinai (Mosaic) covenant was made through Moses, when God gave the Torah to the Israelites.

questions.q: What event does the festival of Pesach (Passover) commemorate?
options: The Exodus from slavery in Egypt
questions.explain: Pesach commemorates the Israelites' escape from slavery in Egypt under Moses.

questions.q: During Sukkot, what do many Jewish families build and eat in?
questions.explain: During Sukkot families build a sukkah, a temporary hut recalling the Israelites' time in the wilderness.

questions.q: What is the Torah?
options: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible
questions.explain: The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, central to Jewish teaching and law.

questions.q: Which festival is known as the Jewish Day of Atonement?
questions.explain: Yom Kippur is the Day of Atonement, the holiest day in the Jewish year, marked by fasting and prayer.

questions.q: What is the Brit Milah in Judaism?
options: The reading from the Torah scroll
The circumcision of a baby boy, usually on the eighth day
questions.explain: Brit Milah is the circumcision of a baby boy on the eighth day, marking the covenant with Abraham.

questions.q: In Judaism, the Messiah is generally understood to be:
options: A symbol with no personal meaning
A future anointed leader who has not yet come
questions.explain: Most Jews believe the Messiah is a future human leader, anointed by God, who has not yet arrived.

questions.q: Which animal is considered NOT kosher and therefore forbidden to eat?
questions.explain: Pork is not kosher because pigs do not chew the cud, so it is forbidden under Jewish dietary law.

questions.q: Which patriarch was renamed Israel and had twelve sons?
questions.explain: Jacob was renamed Israel, and his twelve sons became the ancestors of the twelve tribes.
